text:
An electrical power line, having a total
resistance of 2 $\Omega$, delivers 1 kW at 220 V. The
efficiency of the transmission line is
approximately :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $η=\frac{P_{out}}{(P_{out}+P_{loss})}\times 100$

Given, P= $vi=10^{3}$

$\therefore$ $i=\frac{1000}{220}$ = $\frac{50}{11}$ A

Power $loss=i^{2}R=\left (\frac{50}{11}\right )^{2}\times 2$

$\therefore$ efficiency $=\frac{1000}{1000+i^{2}R}\times 100=96%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
A wheel is rotating freely with an angular speed
$ω$ on a shaft. The moment of inertia of the
wheel is I and the moment of inertia of the
shaft is negligible. Another wheel of moment of
inertia 3I initially at rest is suddenly coupled to
the same shaft. The resultant fractional loss in
the kinetic energy of the system is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Applying Angular Momentum conservation 

$Iω=(I+3I)ω^{'}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω^{'}=\frac{Iω}{4I}=\frac{ω}{4}$

$k_{i}=\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}$

$k_{f}=\frac{1}{2}(4I)(ω^{'})^{2}$

$=2I\left (\frac{ω}{4}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{8}Iω^{2}$

Fractional loss $=\frac{K_{i}-K_{f}}{K_{i}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}-\frac{1}{8}Iω^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}}$

= $\frac{\frac{3}{8}Iω^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}}=\frac{3}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
A helicopter rises from rest on the ground
vertically upwards with a constant acceleration
g. A food packet is dropped from the helicopter
when it is at a height h. The time taken by the
packet to reach the ground is close to :

[g is the
acceleration due to gravity]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The helicopter starts from rest with an upward acceleration $g$, so at height $h$ its speed is

$v=\sqrt{0+2gh}=\sqrt{2gh}\text{(upwards)}$

A packet released from the helicopter has the helicopter's velocity at that instant, so it starts with $\sqrt{2gh}$ upwards and then moves under gravity alone, with acceleration $g$ downwards.


[IMG]

Taking upwards as positive, the displacement of the packet until it reaches the ground is $-h$:

$-h=\sqrt{2gh}t-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\Rightarrow gt^{2}-2\sqrt{2gh}t-2h=0$

Keeping the positive root,

$t=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2gh}+\sqrt{8gh+8gh}}{2g}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2gh}+4\sqrt{gh}}{2g}=\left (\sqrt{2}+2\right )\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}}\approx 3.4\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
Assume that the displacement(s) of air is
proportional to the pressure difference ($\Delta$p)
created by a sound wave. Displacement (s)
further depends on the speed of sound (v),
density of air ($ρ$) and the frequency (f). If
$\Delta$p ~ 10 Pa, v ~ 300 m/s, $ρ$ ~ $1 kg/m^{3}$ and f ~ 1000 Hz,
then s will be of the order of (take the
multiplicative constant to be 1) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, S $\propto$ $\Delta$p

and Proportionality constant = 1

We know, 

$\Delta$p = S$β$k

= $ρv^{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{ω}{v}\times S$

= $ρvωS$

$\therefore$ S = $\frac{\Delta p}{ρvω}$

= $\frac{\Delta p}{ρv2πf}$

= $\frac{\Delta p}{ρvf}$ 

[As Proportionality constant = 1 so assume 2$π$ = 1]

$=\frac{10}{1\times 300\times 1000}$

$=\frac{1}{30}mm$

$\approx \frac{3}{100}mm$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
A balloon is moving up in air vertically above a
point A on the ground. When it is at a height $h_{1}$,
a girl standing at a distance d (point B) from A
(see figure) sees it at an angle $45^{o}$ with respect
to the vertical. When the balloon climbs up a
further height $h_{2}$, it is seen at an angle $60^{o}$ with
respect to the vertical if the girl moves further
by a distance 2.464 d (point C). Then the height
$h_{2}$ is (given $\tan  30^{o} = 0.5774)$

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


From $\Delta ABD$

$\tan 45=\frac{h_{1}}{d}$

$\Rightarrow 1=\frac{h_{1}}{d}$

$\Rightarrow h_{1}=d$

From $\Delta ACE$

$\tan 30=\frac{h_{1}+h_{2}}{d+2.464d}$

$\Rightarrow$ $0.5774=\frac{d+h_{2}}{3.464d}$

$\Rightarrow$ $d+h_{2}=0.5774\times 3.464\times d$

$\Rightarrow$ $h_{2}=2.0001136d-d$

$\Rightarrow$ $h_{2}=2.000d-d=d$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

solution.body:
[IMG]


We know, $τ=MB\sin θ$

Here $M = IA = I(2a)^{2} = 4a^{2}I$

B = $\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}$

Angle between B and $M = 90^{o}$

$\therefore$ $τ=\left (4a^{2}I\right )\left (\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\right )\sin 90^{\circ }$

= $\frac{2μ_{0}I^{2}a^{2}}{πb}$

text:
A particle of mass 200 MeV$/c^{2}$ collides with a
hydrogen atom at rest. Soon after the collision
the particle comes to rest, and the atom
recoils and goes to its first excited state. The
initial kinetic energy of the particle (in eV) is

$\frac{N}{4}$. The value of N is :

(Given the mass of the hydrogen atom to be 1
GeV$/c^{2}) ______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $m_{$particle} =  200 MeV$/c^{2} = m($Assume)

and $m_{H} = 1$
GeV$/c^{2} = 1000$ MeV$/c^{2} = 5$ $\times$ 200 = 5m

Applying momentum conservation,

$p_{i} = p_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $mv_{0}$
 + 0 = 0 + 5 mv'

$\Rightarrow$ v' = $\frac{v_{0}}{5}$

Initial kinetic energy, $k_{i} =$ $\frac{1}{2}mv_{0}^{2}$

Final kinetic energy, $k_{f} =$ $\frac{1}{2}(5m)\left (\frac{v_{0}}{5}\right )^{2}$

$\therefore$ Loss in KE

= $\frac{1}{2}mv_{0}^{2}$ - $\frac{1}{2}(5m)\left (\frac{v_{0}}{5}\right )^{2}$

= $\frac{4}{5}\left (\frac{1}{2}mv_{0}^{2}\right )$ = $\frac{4}{5}(k_{i})$

This lost energy is used by the hydrogen atom to move from ground state to the first excited state. We know the the energy required by the hydrogen atom to move from ground state to first excited state is 10.2 eV.

$\therefore$ $\frac{4}{5}(k_{i})$ = 10.2

$\Rightarrow$ $k_{i} =$ $\frac{5\times 10.2}{4}=\frac{51}{4}$

$\therefore$ N = 51
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
A compound microscope consists of an
objective lens of focal length 1 cm and an
eyepiece of focal length 5 cm with a separation
of 10 cm.

The distance between an object and the
objective lens, at which the strain on the eye is
minimum is $\frac{n}{40}$ cm. The value of n is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Given, $L = |v_{0}| + |u_{e}| = 10 cm$

$(v_{e} =$ $\infty$)

$\frac{1}{v_{e}}-\frac{1}{u_{e}}=\frac{1}{f_{e}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\infty }-\frac{1}{u_{e}}=\frac{1}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $u_{e} = -5$

$\Rightarrow$ $|u_{e}| = 5 cm$

$\therefore$ $|v_{0}| + 5 = 10 cm$

$\Rightarrow$ $|v_{0}| = 5 cm$

For objective, $v_{0} = 5 cm, f_{0} = 1 cm$

$\frac{1}{v_{0}}-\frac{1}{u_{0}}=\frac{1}{f_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{u_{0}}=\frac{1}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $u_{0} =$ $-\frac{5}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|u_{0}| =$ $\frac{5}{4}$ = $\frac{50}{40}$ = $\frac{n}{40}$

$\therefore$ n = 50
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot
